operator.model: 16 low-order modes (E1,B1,E2,B2; Frobenius-orthonormal STF chart); CAT = catalogue covariance, TMPL = scan-law ellipse M^-1 det-matched to catalogue; spurious response from a unit-amplitude per-pixel (nside16) white systematic vector along the major-information scan axis vs isotropic-direction control

interpretation: Formal mode errors are insensitive to the covariance orientation model: replacing the catalogue ellipse by the det-matched scan-law ellipse changes mode sd by -2.6% to +3.9%.

A pixel-scale white systematic of 1 mas/yr per pixel moves the low-order modes by ~65-100 formal sd; aligning it with the scan axis raises this by only ~10-25% over an isotropic control. Pixel-scale systematic amplitude, not scan orientation, dominates; a systematic floor on E/B l<=2 modes is set by the (unknown) amplitude of correlated pixel-scale errors, not by statistics.
The bias is a model response, not an estimate of the real DR3 systematic amplitude, which is not constrained here.

claims.claim: Scan-aware and catalogue covariances give the same formal low-order mode errors to within ~4%.
claims.limit: dispersion of the catalogue per-source ellipse around the pixel median not modelled; l>=3 excluded

claims.claim: Scan-aligned pixel-scale systematics project onto l<=2 E/B modes ~10-25% more strongly than isotropic ones.
claims.limit: white per-pixel toy systematic; no correlation length; real DR3 systematic amplitude not determined; 100 draws
